claims.claim: The sell-side lifecycle is a seven-phase rail: Phase 0 Mandate & origination, 1 Preparation, 2 Marketing & outreach, 3 First-round bids, 4 Diligence & second round, 5 Negotiation & signing, 6 Closing & post-close.
claims.vsCanon: Canonical model is five phases (Origination Qualification & Mandate / Preparation & Market Readiness / Marketing & First-Round Bids / Diligence LOI & Definitive Docs / Signing Closing & Post-Close); the doc adds a Phase 0 and splits marketing from first-round bids and negotiation/signing from closing.

claims.claim: The working step count is ~82 skills/apps (per Vision 2-pager v1.1), with Storm quoted as 'we currently have 92' of ~100 steps.
claims.vsCanon: Canonical is now Seq 1-65 steps plus 21 horizontal always-on apps; the 82/92 figures predate the July v2 enumeration.

claims.claim: Each step carries one of three actor values (RailActor in PR #62): human, agent, or both, where 'both' = agent drafts + human signs off.
claims.vsCanon: Canonical execution classes are four: A / A+H / H+A / H — the doc's single 'both' value collapses the A+H (agent-leads) vs H+A (human-leads) distinction.
claims.sourceRef: deal-lifecycle-rails.md § Human vs agent — the allocation rule

claims.claim: A non-sequential always-on layer runs across the rail: four deal-scoped capabilities (ask-the-deal, pre-send QC, comms capture, weekly update) plus two portfolio-scoped (morning digest, staffing/deal-intensity view).
claims.vsCanon: Agrees on the concept of a horizontal always-on layer but enumerates only 6 capabilities vs the canonical 21 horizontal always-on apps.

claims.claim: Phase 0 (Mandate & origination) comprises six steps: win the mandate (pitch), KYC/conflicts/FINRA/MNPI screen, create deal + mint code name, stand up the deal team, connect email/calendar/files/CRM, assign responsibilities + limits.
claims.vsCanon: Canonical gate 0 is exactly 4 pre-deal actions (code name, team/permissions, notify compliance/mgmt, lifecycle entry point); the doc covers code name + team but lacks notify-compliance/mgmt and lifecycle-entry-point, and adds pitch/connectors/responsibility-assignment which are not gate-0 actions.

claims.claim: The MVP is Layer 0 — a guided sequential checklist walking a human open-to-close (deal team standup, connectors, assign responsibilities) — with Layer 1 (allocation) and Layer 2 (autonomy) deliberately deferred.
claims.vsCanon: Consistent with the canonical gradual-automation posture (rails fixed, per-step mode migrates from human toward agent as trust builds).
claims.sourceRef: deal-lifecycle-rails.md § Three layers — do not build them all at once

claims.claim: Human-vs-agent allocation is decided by stakes, implemented in the orchestrator: low-stakes internal steps run agent-solo with zero gates; high-stakes/external steps pause for human plan-confirm and sign-off before anything leaves the firm.
claims.vsCanon: Matches the canonical invariant (agents draft/propose; humans gate external/irreversible actions) and the reversible-vs-irreversible risk-tier rule.
claims.sourceRef: deal-lifecycle-rails.md § Human vs agent — the allocation rule

claims.claim: Per-step build-status ground truth: each rail step is tagged ✅ real on develop / 🟡 schema-only / 🔴 not built, mapped to concrete repo mechanisms (compliance/screen.ts, POST /api/v1/deals, documents.min_phase, workflows/teaser.ts, audit_log #49, legal hold #60, dealRail.ts PR #62).
claims.vsCanon: Not covered by canon or the new sources — the only step-by-step map of the canonical process onto what actually exists in code.
claims.sourceRef: deal-lifecycle-rails.md § The rail (status legend + Today columns) + § Source grounding

claims.claim: Connectors are the precondition for most agent steps; recommendation is files/data-room first (compliance envelope ~80% built: classification, min_phase, MNPI screen, audit, legal hold), email second (heaviest envelope: privilege, personal data, MNPI at inbox scale).
claims.vsCanon: Canon records connectors as deferred/'too early'; this doc adds the value-vs-risk-vs-envelope analysis and a concrete files-first sequencing recommendation absent from the newer sources.

claims.claim: Semantic phase labels are not yet defined in code — the repo gates documents by numeric phase (documents.min_phase, deal status intake→active→paused→closed) and the phase names are a proposed product layer awaiting a decision.
claims.vsCanon: A live open question the canonical facts now answer (five phases): flags exactly where code must be re-labeled to the canonical phase cut.
claims.sourceRef: deal-lifecycle-rails.md § The rail (intro paragraph) + § Open questions #1

claims.claim: Draft the CIM / management presentation is a rail step in the 'want to close' bucket (future workflow; 'Rogo's highest-leverage skill').
claims.vsCanon: Canon explicitly defers CIM authoring and management-presentation drafting (Founders §4.5; Vision2p 'HOW IT'S USED' — starting with judgment-heavy authoring is 'insanely stupid'); the doc treats it as a roadmap gap to close.

claims.claim: The sandbox ships with exactly five skills (financial-performance, acquirer-fit, culture-signal, deal-readiness free; synergy-engine Pro-locked), each a draggable unit rendering a panel and visibly routing through compliance.
claims.vsCanon: Sandbox-demo catalogue, self-declared provisional pending 06-research; canonical 'skill' is now one of the Seq 1-65 step-apps (plus 21 horizontal apps), not a draggable panel unit — the two taxonomies are disjoint.

claims.claim: Skill ids, premium flags, and panel values are a hard code contract with src/lib/api/types.ts and src/lib/api/fixtures.ts; ids must not be renamed without updating both.
claims.vsCanon: Pure engineering contract for the shipped sandbox front-end; no equivalent in canon or the new sources, and load-bearing for anyone touching the sandbox.

claims.claim: Rogo's 2026-06-29 capability surface (from confidential Ignatious materials): persistent Enhanced Projects workspaces up to 10k files, house-style 'the Ignatious way' skills, buyer lists/screening, 3-statement models, live recurring scheduled digests, on-brand outputs, document playbook.
claims.vsCanon: Matches and extends canon's Rogo-1p reading (document-Q&A workspace roadmapping Conductia's territory); adds the management-presentation skill walkthrough not in the one-pager.

claims.claim: Deliberately-skip bucket: 3-statement model building ('we are a decision surface, not a modeling tool'), transcript-to-minutes/generic productivity, generic NDA/LOI contract turns.
claims.vsCanon: Aligned with canon's protected v1 exclusions and deferred-applications rationale (no financial-model building; final numbers from a deterministic model of record, not an LLM).

claims.claim: Want-to-close bucket includes extending DraftAgent beyond the teaser to CIM/buyer-deck drafting and a house-style firm-template skill, once a real data room exists.
claims.vsCanon: In tension with canon's explicit deferral of CIM authoring (Founders §4.5; RTS-notes; Vision2p) — the doc itself flags buckets as 'a starting proposal, not a decided roadmap' pending the Storm session.
claims.sourceRef: rogo-skills-gap-map.md § Want to close + § Honest caveats

claims.claim: Already-ahead bucket: pre-send compliance gate (COMPLIANCE_SCREEN + ComplianceSupervisor, 'they tell you after, we stop it before'), physically append-only audit trail (#58), and governed autonomy via the stakes split (AWAIT_PLAN_CONFIRM / AWAIT_SIGNOFF).
claims.vsCanon: Matches canon's moat location (Pre-Send QC screen, approval/gate engine, append-only AuditEvent as highest-moat owned components; Rogo has no compliance layer).

claims.claim: The product is a navigable platform with four destinations (Mandate /, Acquirers, Deep-dive workspace, Team 'compliance theatre', Skills catalogue) under persistent chrome (AppHeader/AppNav, CommandBar, single ComplianceRibbon).

claims.vsCanon: Consistent with canonical compliance-first posture (every action screened before release; deterministic gates); the specific KYC→FINRA→MNPI cascade is the repo's concrete implementation of gate-0-style screening.

claims.claim: Skill access is the tier signal and upgrading (the synergy-engine paywall on drop) is the explicit revenue line.
claims.vsCanon: Sandbox monetization demo that contradicts canonical pricing: two-layer hybrid with no seats/tiers (platform access fee + deal-linked component, priced against labor value / NLVC, never per-skill upgrades).

claims.claim: A prior 7-step linear demo spine (ColdOpen → Intent → Landscape → DeepDive → ComplianceTheatre → PitchCta) was retired in Phase F (commit fbf10a0, 2026-05-20); the platform replaced the spine and explicit navigation replaced auto-advance.

CIM/management-presentation drafting: deal-lifecycle-rails.md (Phase 1 row) and rogo-skills-gap-map.md (§ Want to close) place CIM/mgmt-presentation drafting on the roadmap as a gap to close vs canon's explicit deferral of CIM authoring and management-presentation drafting (Founders §4.5; Vision2p 'HOW IT'S USED').

notes: deal-lifecycle-rails.md is the only artifact mapping the canonical process onto repo reality: per-step ✅/🟡/🔴 build-status against concrete code (compliance/screen.ts, /api/v1/deals, documents.min_phase, workflows/teaser.ts, audit_log #49, legal hold #60, dealRail.ts + DealRail.tsx PR #62). The new docx sources define the process; only this doc says what of it exists. Preserve, then relabel to the canonical 5 phases / Seq 1-65.

deal-lifecycle-rails.md's connectors analysis (files/data-room first, email second, with the five-part compliance envelope: scope, screen-on-ingest, gate, audit, retain) is a sequencing recommendation with no equivalent in the newer sources.

deal-lifecycle-rails.md's three-layer build model (Layer 0 checklist → Layer 1 allocation → Layer 2 autonomy) and the stakes-based allocation rule already implemented in the orchestrator operationalize the canonical gradual-automation posture in engineering terms.

rogo-skills-gap-map.md carries competitive intelligence from confidential 2026-06-29 Rogo-for-Ignatious materials (management-presentation skill walkthrough; Enhanced Projects at 10k-file scale; live scheduled digests) beyond what the Rogo one-pager in canon contains, plus a build/skip/already-ahead triage.

skills-catalog.md and experience-spine.md are sandbox-build contracts (skill-id ↔ fixtures.ts hard contract; single ComplianceRibbon mount; KYC→FINRA→MNPI compliance boot; the retired 7-step spine's historical record) — needed by anyone touching the shipped front-end, even after the product model supersedes them.

Coverage gap (not a conflict): none of the four docs mention skip-with-approval, edit-after-complete with versioned outputs, or the 21-horizontal-app enumeration by name — these canonical mechanics arrive only with the July v2 sources and have no repo-doc counterpart yet.
